Ohio Cannabis and Hemp Research — Parts 0–12

Run 1 (Parts 0–6, accessed 28 October 2026) and Run 2 (Parts 7–12, accessed 28–29 October 2026) in one document. Every value is carried with its source as compiled; hedges, conflicts and open questions are preserved, not smoothed over. The compiler’s combined research notes for both runs appear first in the report below — read them before relying on any single figure.

Parts 0–12 · 13 parts 57 tables 523 source links in text 458 Verify mentions preserved Federal baseline: medical Schedule III / adult-use Schedule I (28 Apr 2026)

Chapter 3780 is gone

SB 56 repealed the voter-enacted adult-use chapter and consolidated medical and adult-use law into a rewritten ORC Chapter 3796, effective 20 March 2026. Current adult-use rules in this dossier are SB 56 amendments unless expressly carried over unchanged.

Ohio moved on hemp before the federal dates

From 20 March 2026, Ohio’s hemp definition already excludes final products above 0.4 mg combined total THC per container — the figure federal law reaches after 11 December 2026 — and the Governor line-item vetoed the hemp-beverage grace period, so there is no Ohio grace period running to December.

Still open — do not treat as settled

No official statewide opt-out list or map, no DCC enforcement register, and no social-equity certification list were located in either run. The testing-lab census (6 vs 7 vs 8) and several figures in the conflicts log remain unresolved; each is flagged in place.

Ohio Cannabis and Hemp Research — Parts 0–12 — AUDITED

Last audited: 30 October 2026. This is the independent audit and corrected rewrite of the attached Parts 0–12 report. The auditor did not write the original. Primary sources only were used to confirm or correct a claim: codes.ohio.gov (Ohio Revised Code Chapters 3780, 3796 and 928, and other chapters cited), the Ohio Administrative Code, legislature.ohio.gov / Legislative Service Commission, the Division of Cannabis Control (DCC), the State Medical Board and Board of Pharmacy, the Ohio Department of Agriculture (ODA), the Ohio Department of Taxation, the Governor's executive orders, the Ohio Secretary of State, court records, and official county, city, village and township codes. News, law-firm blogs, trade press and AI summaries were not used to confirm anything; where only such a source exists the verdict is Unverified.

Federal baseline applied as given, not re-audited. Under the final rule at 91 FR 22714 (effective 28 April 2026), FDA-approved cannabis products and state-licensed medical marijuana are Schedule III; all other marijuana, including all adult-use, remains Schedule I; the broader 2024 rescheduling proposal is not final. IRS 280E relief therefore applies to medical Schedule III activity only; adult-use activity remains fully subject to 280E, and dual (medical + adult-use) licensees must split their activity. Hemp: Public Law 119-37 §781 takes legal effect 12 November 2026, but Public Law 119-103 §2019 limits it until 11 December 2026 to only the provisions excluding cannabinoids that are not naturally produced or are synthesised; the full total-THC definition and 0.4 mg per container cap apply after 11 December 2026. USDA has delayed enforcement of the DEA-registered-laboratory hemp testing requirement until 31 December 2026. The federal medical-marijuana appropriations rider is in force through 11 December 2026. No federal cannabis banking law has been enacted. Any statement in the original contradicting this baseline has been corrected to match it. Ohio law is not thereby changed: ORC 3796.01(C) still says, for purposes of Chapter 3796 only, marijuana is Schedule II — a third, Ohio-only label that must not be published as "Ohio now calls medical marijuana Schedule III."

Corrected current snapshot — use these figures, not the superseded ones in dated notes below

  • DCC By the Numbers, last updated 26 October 2026 (direct file: DCC_Update_By_The_Numbers.pdf): 233 operating dual-use dispensaries + 47 provisional = 280 (not 233 + 47 = 279); headroom to the 400 cap is 120, not 121; 37 cultivators (23 Level I + 14 Level II), 45 processors, 6 testing laboratories, 9,916 individuals with active employee licences (not 9,916).
  • Patients/caregivers as of 30 September 2026 in the same PDF: 1,309,064 recommendations; 476,589 registered patients (not 476,589 at 31 Aug); 26,415 veteran, 27,181 indigent, 1,583 terminal-diagnosis; 73,396 with both active registration and active recommendation (not 73,396); 440,441 unique purchasers (OARRS, not 440,441); 42,922 registered caregivers (not 42,922); 484 certificates to recommend as of 14 October 2026. Never quote "registered" (476,589) as the active patient population (73,396).
  • Sales as of 10 October 2026 in the same PDF: non-medical $1,987,109,580 + medical $2,438,844,126 = $4,425,955,615; 681,864 lbs plant material; 74,647,313 manufactured units; 51,653,158 receipts. Caveat, verified by arithmetic on the PDF's own components: the printed dollar total is $1,909 above the sum of its components, pounds 480 above, units 342 above, receipts 5,834 above. Quote printed totals; do not "fix" them to component sums. Only the DCC workbook can explain the gap.
  • Processor fees, OAC 1301:18-2-09 (effective 8 October 2026): $40,000 issuance / $50,000 renewal. The LSC $90,000 / $100,000 figures are superseded and must not appear as current fees anywhere. Note the category correction: 1301:18-2-09 is the DCC cannabis processor schedule. It is not the ODA hemp-processing schedule, which is OAC 901:14-2-04 (see Part 7 rows).
  • Employee badges survive: OAC 1301:18-2-09(A)(4) still prescribes $100 initial and $100 renewal badge fees, and DCC still counts 9,916 active employee licences. The secondary claim that SB 56 eliminated employee licences is not supported by the current rule or DCC counts.
  • Tax distribution: HB 96 (enacted) repealed the Issue 2 allocations and set 64% General Revenue Fund / 36% Host Community Cannabis Fund; SB 56 (signed 19 December 2025, effective 20 March 2026) recodified that 64/36 split at ORC 3796.40(F) with monthly distribution. Do not attribute creation of 64/36 to SB 56. The former Issue 2 split (36% social equity / 36% host / 25% substance abuse / 3% DCC–Tax Commissioner, quarterly) is history only. SB 56 §12 appropriated $47.5m FY 2026 and $49.0m FY 2027 for the Host Community Cannabis Fund; DCC operating costs are fee-funded into Fund 5SY0, not GRF-funded as the original implied.
  • No personal phone or email for an individual licence holder was found in Parts 4–6, and none is reproduced in this rewrite. The only phone in those parts is the DCC agency line 1-833-464-6627. Named individuals elsewhere are public officials. No redaction was otherwise required.

Part 1 — Audit table

Verdicts: Confirmed = primary source supports it as written. Corrected = primary source supports a different wording, given in the last column. Removed = wrong and no correct version found (none of the headline claims required removal; wrong figures are replaced, not left standing). Unverified = only a secondary source exists, or the primary source was not opened; the flag is kept. Dated historical snapshots (e.g. January 2025, June 2026) are retained only where they are explicitly labelled as dated snapshots, never as current figures.

Part 2, §2.8 federal hemp conformityNo Ohio official response to PL 119-37 §781 / PL 119-103 §2019 located; whether Ohio conforms its Ch. 928 definition to the post-11-Dec federal total-THC definition is VerifyConfirmed as a negative findingORC 928.01 (in force 20 Mar 2026; no post-Dec conformity amendment shown)Keep flagged. Part 7, §§7.2/7.6 research exemption"Dept/university may cultivate/process for research without a licence" (stated jointly)Corrected — split itORC 928.02(A)(4)–(5); 7 CFR 990.21(d)(1)Processing research exemption survives on statute text — ORC 928.02(A)(5), "as authorized by the director," with no cultivation-programme condition. Location/coordinate requirement: 990.21(a)(3) as opened lists contact + criminal history only; keep the location-reporting sentence only with [Verify] against the HeMP application form and 7 CFR 990.23/990.71, not as a 990.21 quote. Delete the $25–$100 FBI range (secondary only, unverified). Sampling rewrite: "Under 990.24 a sampling agent must collect samples no more than 30 days before anticipated harvest, from flowering tops (top 5–8 inches of main stem/terminal bud/central cola), at 95% confidence that ≤1% of plants exceed the acceptable level; the crop must not be harvested before sampling, and must be harvested within 30 days after sampling (990.26) or be resampled. The federal test is for total delta-9 THC (990.24(a), 990.1 'acceptable hemp THC level'), with post-decarboxylation/similarly reliable methods that account for THCA conversion (990.25(g)) and measurement of uncertainty: a lot passes if the uncertainty range includes 0.3% or less. Non-compliant lots are disposed of/remediated under 990.27." DEA-lab enforcement delay to 31 Dec 2026 is taken as given federal baseline, not re-audited here. Codified current (OAC 901:14-2-04, eff. 31 Jan 2020, still shown on codes.ohio.gov): $100 application per application; per site per year $500 raw grain, $500 raw fibre, $3,000 raw floral, $500 wholesale cannabinoid food/supplement/cosmetic, $250 retail in same categories; fees non-refundable. Proposed amendment (RSFA, filed 25 Aug 2026, PH_OF_A — public-hearing original, not a final filing): $100 application; $3,000 extraction of cannabinoids; $500 wholesale-or-retail (grain/fibre fees removed; single wholesale-or-retail fee). Do not quote the RSFA schedule as current until a final filing + effective date is found on Register of Ohio/JCARR. The report's "effective date [Verify]" understates this: filing date ≠ effective date, and codified text contradicts "current" use. 1301:18-2-09 is the DCC cannabis fee schedule (Division of Cannabis Control, Dept. of Commerce), eff. 8 Oct 2026: processor initial application $10,000; certificate issuance $40,000; renewal $50,000; badges $100 initial/renewal. It therefore does resolve the Run 1 cannabis-processor conflict in favour of OAC over LSC — but it has nothing to do with ODA hemp processing fees. Any Part 7 text importing $40,000/$50,000 as a hemp fee must be removed.

Part 10, §10.2 hemp shipmentsFarm Bill §10114: (a) nothing prohibits interstate commerce of hemp/hemp products; (b) no State/Tribe shall prohibit transportation/shipment of compliant hemp through the State. Codified at 7 U.S.C. §§1639o–1639p; transit rule at §1639o; Ohio-grown (USDA) hemp shipped out lawful if it meets destination + federal definitions; no separate Ohio "export" licence in Ch. 928 as read; through-shipment federal transit protection; into Ohio for sale must meet ORC 928.01 (total THC incl. THCA ≤0.3% plant; final product ≤0.4 mg/container; no non-natural or synthesised-outside-plant cannabinoids); intoxicating hemp (delta-8, THCA flower, >0.4 mg beverages/gummies) into Ohio: not hemp in Ohio; N.D. Ohio injunctions create no general import rightCorrected (citation); Confirmed (substance and 928.01 thresholds + direction analysis); "no import/export licence" = none located7 U.S.C. §1639o (definitions; Interstate Commerce note: Pub. L. 115-334 §10114); ORC 928.01 (eff. 20 Mar 2026)Correct to: "Pub. L. 115-334 §10114, set out as a note to 7 U.S.C. §1639o. §1639o itself defines 'hemp'; §1639p governs state/tribal plans and at (a)(3)(A) preserves more-stringent state production laws." Keep the report's transit-vs-sale analysis: the bar is on prohibiting through-shipment of subtitle-G-compliant hemp; it does not compel a state to permit sale/possession-for-sale in-state of a product the state lawfully regulates more stringently, and it does not protect a product that is not "hemp" under the applicable definition. OAC 901:14 transport/storage text post-SB 56: keep Verify (928.04 transport framework was not opened line-by-line here).

Add (H): "A provisional license issued under this section is not transferable" — this strengthens §11.2.5's "no standalone transfer" point. Also (F): ≥15% of cultivator/processor/lab licences to Ohio-resident US citizens in the listed economically disadvantaged groups (≥51% owned/controlled) — a social-equity-type provision the report's Part 11 does not mention; do not conflate it with a separate "cannabis social equity and jobs programme" without checking the current programme rules. 7-01 confirmed verbatim, including (D)(2) "laboratory testing, research, and development" — that is R&D within a testing licence, not a university research licence. 7-04/7-05/7-06: not re-opened in the Parts 11–12 audit. Part 11, §11.2 licence rulesFour licence types only; dispensary cap 400; ownership caps 8/1/1, ORC 3796.05; ORC 3796.14 discipline, 90/91-day summary-suspension rule; ORC 3796.15 enforcement/sealing, OAC 1301:18-9-05 discipline powers; renewals OAC 1301:18-2-08 (eff. 20 Dec 2024): cultivator/processor annual, lab/dispensary biennial, 30-day advance filing, 30-day max suspension then deemed revoked; fees OAC 1301:18-2-09 (eff. 8 Oct 2026) table, badges $100, change of ownership $1,000, name $500, location $1,000, major modification $1,000, product registration $100, advertising review $100; transfers/ownership changes: no standalone licence sale, DCC approval required (secondary guidance summaries); relocation OAC 1301:18-3-02: prior DCC approval, same district + 1-mile rule for dispensaries, 90-day transition, destruction of leftovers under 3-12; surrender/revocation wind-down, proposed OAC 1301:18-3-17 "Discontinuing Business" (90 days' notice); insurance/bonding OAC 1301:18-3-08: CGL + products liability (no dollar limit stated) + escrow/bond L1 $750k / L2 $75k / processor $250k / lab $75k / dispensary $50k, reductions to $250k/$25k/$75k/$25k/$15k after 1 yr, termination after 3 yrsConfirmed (four types, cap, ownership, 3796.15 statute, renewals, fees, insurance/bonding amounts); Corrected (3796.14 scope, $50,000 cap attribution); Unverified (transfers procedure, relocation, surrender/wind-down, 9-05 detail)ORC 3796.05; ORC 3796.14; ORC 3796.15; OAC 1301:18-2-08; OAC 1301:18-2-09; OAC 1301:18-3-083796.05(B)(1) "Not more than four hundred licensed dispensaries"; (B)(2) 18-month provisional-to-certificate clock + max two 6-month good-faith extensions; (B)(4) no new/relocated dispensary within 1 mile of another or at a Chapter 4303 liquor-permit premises; (C) 8/1/1 caps — all confirmed. The old "5 dispensaries" figure is superseded. 3796.14: 90/91-day passage confirmed verbatim, but its scope is narrower than the report states: (A)(4) says "The division shall suspend a dispensary license without prior hearing only if it finds clear and convincing evidence that continued distribution … presents a danger of immediate and serious harm to others" and the suspension lifts on the 91st day if no final adjudication order within 90 days after the hearing. Do not generalise it to all licence types. Also (A)(3): civil penalty "in an amount to be determined by the division" — the $50,000-per-violation cap is a rule (OAC 1301:18-9-05) figure, not the statute's cap. 3796.15 confirmed verbatim: DCC + Ohio Investigative Unit enforce; on suspension/revocation/refusal + clear-and-convincing immediate-serious-harm finding, DCC may seal all medical/adult-use/homegrown marijuana in the holder's possession/custody/control; no disposal until Chapter 119 appeal rights exhausted, except a court may order sale of perishable marijuana with proceeds deposited with the court. OAC 1301:18-9-05's detailed list was not re-opened — retain the report's citation, and note its text still cites repealed Chapter 3780. Renewals confirmed verbatim, including on deemed revocation: permanently cease operations, destroy the certificate and all affiliated employee badges. Fees confirmed verbatim, including lab renewal "$20,000 per year, which may be paid in one sum of $40,000" and dispensary "$35,000 per year … $70,000" for two years. Processor issuance $40,000 / renewal $50,000 supersedes the $90,000/$100,000 secondary figures. Transfers: the $1,000 change-of-ownership fee is confirmed, but the "written approval before effectiveness / drafts before execution" procedure is not in the fee rule — do not cite it as rule text; confirm in DCC Ownership, Control, and Financial Interest Guidance and the codified OAC change-of-ownership rule, if any. Relocation: not re-opened; retain the report's summary and its flag that the rule cites OAC 1301:18-7-02, which the report says returned "Number Not Found." Surrender: the report is right not to cite 3-17 as current law (it says "Number Not Found"). 3-15 itself was not opened in Run 2 or this audit — keep flagged. Insurance/bonding: amounts, 1-year reduction conditions (fully operational without substantial interruption + demonstrated compliance), and 3-year termination conditions confirmed verbatim. Retain the ambiguity flag on (F): it says DCC will approve a licensee "to further reduce its financial responsibility in the amount outlined in paragraph (D)" after 2 consecutive years — the text repeats the (D) amounts, it does not clearly state a second step-down by the same amounts. Do not present a two-step ladder as settled. The "one bond per dual-use licence" point remains secondary DCC-guidance summary only.

Part 11, §11.8 employment / background checksEmployment ORC 3796.28: no duty to permit/accommodate, employer may refuse to hire/discharge/discipline, drug-testing/drug-free/zero-tolerance policies permitted, DOT/federal rules unaffected, just-cause unemployment consequence, no 4112.02(A)/(D)/(E) violation if policy-based; applicant background checks ORC 3796.12: BCI, plus FBI where 5-year Ohio residency not shown, denial for failure to complete/forward/instruct; employee background checks ORC 3796.13: ORC 4776.01–4776.04 compliance, no employment unless report shows no disqualifying offence, provisional employment max 3 months, renewable once for 3 months; employee badges $100 initial and $100 renewal (all designations), OAC 1301:18-2-09(A)(4)ConfirmedORC 3796.28; ORC 3796.12; ORC 3796.13; OAC 1301:18-2-093796.28 confirmed verbatim. This confirms the report's "no DCC-mandated employee drug test located" position is consistent with the statute: 3796.28 permits employer testing policies, it does not impose a DCC badging drug test. 3796.12 confirmed verbatim, upgrading Run 2's flag. Note the precise FBI trigger: DCC shall request FBI information if the person does not present 5-year residency proof or evidence BCI already requested FBI information in that period, and may request it even if residency is shown. Reports are not public records (149.43) except to the subject, DCC staff, and courts/hearing officers in licence-denial or programme cases. 3796.13 confirmed verbatim, upgrading Run 2's flag — including that DCC "shall establish standards for provisional employment of individuals who have exigent circumstances," with evidence of 4776 compliance as a minimum. The 90-day provisional badge (Package 5 summary) is a different thing from provisional employment and remains Unverified. Badges confirmed. Responsible-party (1–3 persons, ≥20 hrs/week on premises), owner/officer and employee designations, and the 5-year revocation preclusion, were not re-opened in full — keep those flags.
Part 11, §11.9 researchNo DCC research licence; four licence types; IRB-approved research carve-outs (3796.24(H)(6), 3796.29(B)(3), 3796.30(D))ConfirmedORC 3796.02; ORC 3796.032; ORC 3796.29; ORC 3796.303796.032 confirmed: Chapter 3796 "does not authorize [DCC] to oversee or limit research" at a state university, academic medical center, or private R&D organisation where the research is approved by a listed US government agency/board/center/department/institute (AHRQ, NIH, National Academy of Sciences, CMS, DoD, CDC, VA, DEA, FDA, or an NIH-recognised board). That is a carve-out from DCC oversight, not a DCC licence. CSU/OSU and other university programme claims in the report remain secondary/stale — keep flagged; CSU as a "provisional testing lab" must not be adopted without the DCC list.
Part 12, §12.1 paraphernalia / smoke shopsDispensary paraphernalia sales ORC 3796.20(A)(1)(d); adult-use possession of paraphernalia ORC 3796.221(A)(3); paraphernalia offences/penalties ORC 2925.14(C)(1)–(3): use 4th-degree misdemeanour, sale 2nd-degree (1st if to a juvenile), advertising 2nd-degree, "up to $100 fine" for 2925.141; no statewide "smoke-shop licence"Confirmed (sales/possession); Corrected (offences — material incompleteness); Unverified (smoke-shop absence)ORC 3796.20; ORC 3796.221; ORC 2925.14; ORC 2925.141Offence classes confirmed in 2925.14(F)(1)–(4), but the report's table is incomplete in a material way: 2925.14(D)(2) provides that (C)(1) does not apply to marihuana paraphernalia use/possession — that conduct is instead under 2925.141(C), "illegal use or possession of marihuana drug paraphernalia, a minor misdemeanor" (2925.141(F)(1)), and 2925.141(G) adds that arrest/conviction "does not constitute a criminal record." The report's "up to $100 fine" for 2925.141 is not in 2925.141 — delete it; the section states the class only. The 2925.14(B) factor list in the report is a paraphrase of a longer statutory list (now (B)(1)–(12), eff. 30 Sep 2025, HB 96) — quote it from the current text, not the secondary summary. The CDL/professional-licence gloss remains secondary (see 2925.14(G)/2929.33, not opened here). 3796.20(C)(1) also confirms the visitor point in §12.5: adult-use sale only to a consumer presenting "a current, valid, government-issued identification card demonstrating proof that the adult-use consumer is twenty-one years of age or older" — no residency element appears in that paragraph, so "no Ohio-residency requirement for adult-use purchase" is statute-consistent, but it is an inference from silence; label it as such until 3796.20 is quoted in full. Smoke-shop absence: consistent with the four-type list in 3796.02, but the report's search does not prove no other Ohio retail/zoning licence applies. Keep as "none located," not "none exists." Local smoke-shop zoning/business-licence rules remain Unavailable/local.
Part 12, §12.2 drivingOhio DOES have per se THC driving limits: marihuana ≥10 ng/mL urine / ≥2 ng/mL whole blood or blood serum/plasma, ORC 4511.19(A)(1)(j)(vii); marihuana metabolite per se limits: standalone ≥35 urine / ≥50 blood, with alcohol/drug-of-abuse influence ≥15 urine / ≥5 blood, (A)(1)(j)(viii), "as measured by gas chromatography mass spectrometry"; impairment theory (A)(1)(a); (K) prescription defence; patient status is not alone a basis for a field sobriety test or licence suspension, ORC 3796.24(E); SB 55 (136th GA) would raise whole-blood THC 2→5 ng/mL, drop metabolite/urine/serum per se tiers, add rebuttable-inference tiers — but is NOT law; implied-consent/refusal suspensions (1/2/3 years) and first-offence OVI penalties (72 hrs/DIP, $375–$1,075, 1–3 yr suspension)Confirmed (per se limits, impairment, 3796.24(E), SB 55 status); Corrected (metabolite GCMS qualifier, (K) inference); Unverified (refusal/penalty figures)ORC 4511.19 (eff. 9 Apr 2025, SB 100/HB 37, 135th GA); ORC 3796.24(E); Ohio House SB 55 page; LSC "As Passed by the Senate" analysis (9 Oct 2025)Quote verbatim: "(vii) The person has a concentration of marihuana in the person's urine of at least ten nanograms of marihuana per milliliter of the person's urine or has a concentration of marihuana in the person's whole blood or blood serum or plasma of at least two nanograms of marihuana per milliliter…" Figures for metabolites confirmed, but delete "as measured by gas chromatography mass spectrometry" — that qualifier does not appear in (A)(1)(j)(viii) as published. (viii)(I) requires the person also be "under the influence of alcohol, a drug of abuse, or a combination of them"; (viii)(II) is the standalone 35/50 tier. (K) confirmed verbatim: (A)(1)(j) "does not apply" if both (1) the person "obtained the controlled substance pursuant to a prescription issued by a licensed health professional authorized to prescribe drugs" and (2) took it "in accordance with the health professional's directions." The report's "a medical recommendation is not a prescription, so it does not protect medical use" is an inference from that text, not a sentence in (K) — label it as such. 3796.24(E) confirmed verbatim, including the "independent, factual basis giving reasonable suspicion" requirement. DRE/field-sobriety detail remains secondary — keep flagged. SB 55 status confirmed as: Passed by the Senate; in House Judiciary Committee. Ignore the secondary BillTrack50 "Dead" label. Current 4511.19 limits therefore remain in effect. Refusal/penalty figures: both rest on conflicting secondary summaries. Do not merge the two refusal framings; do not present the first-offence figures as the complete penalty scheme. Confirm at ORC 4511.192 and ORC 4511.19(G).
Part 12, §12.3 expungementORC 2953.321 (SB 56, eff. 20 March 2026) is a petition route, not automatic expungement; "2953.321 does not cover trafficking, cultivation, larger possession, or post-effective-date offences"; general sealing under ORC 2953.32: 1–5 yr waits, F5/ILC example, $0–$400 fees, juvenile "automatic at 23 or 5 years"Confirmed (2953.321 petition-only + limits); Unverified (general sealing details)ORC 2953.321Confirmed: eligible only if, before the section's effective date, the person was a defendant in a dismissed complaint/indictment/information for, or convicted/pleaded guilty to, ORC 2925.11(C)(3)(a) or (C)(7)(a)/(b), or (C)(7)(c)/(d) involving ≤15 g hashish; application to the sentencing court at any time on/after the effective date; $50 fee unless indigent ($30 state / $20 county); hearing 45–90 days after filing; prosecutor may object; court weighs applicant's interest vs legitimate government need. (F) orders expungement and deletion of index references; proceedings "considered not to have occurred." (B) is limited to the offences/amounts above — keep the report's plain-language limit. General sealing: all secondary (law-firm/ExpungeMap/LegalClarity summaries). The report correctly flags them; do not promote them. Likewise "no adult Clean Slate programme" is an absence claim not proven by the searches cited — keep as Unverified, not as a confirmed negative. Confirm at ORC 2953.32 and ORC 2953.36.
Part 12, §§12.4–12.5 lounges, tourism, visitor purchaseNo consumption-lounge licence; public consumption prohibited; adult-use daily dispensing limits: 2.5 oz plant material + ≤15,000 mg total THC, OAC 1301:18-8-08(A)(2) (eff. 28 Aug 2025); medical reciprocity: DCC may enter agreements under ORC 3796.16, no agreement located; interstate transport warning; hotel-room consumption; federal landConfirmed (lounge absence, public-place ban, dispensing limits, reciprocity statute, federal-land bar, possession/transfer limits); Unverified (no agreement, hotel-room lawfulness, ticketed-private-event as "public place")ORC 3796.02; ORC 3796.04; ORC 3796.06; OAC 1301:18-8-08; ORC 3796.16; ORC 3796.221; ORC 3796.24Lounge absence confirmed by the 3796.02 four-type list. Public-place consumption ban confirmed at 3796.04(C)(2)–(3). Smoking/combustion/vaporisation locus confirmed at 3796.06(C)(2): only "privately owned real property that is used primarily for residential or agricultural purposes," and (C)(3) bars it in child-care homes, halfway-house-type facilities, lease-prohibited rentals, and public places/places of employment (ORC 3794.01 definitions). Whether a ticketed private event counts as a "public place" remains Unverified (case law, not statute). Dispensing confirmed verbatim, including the calculation rule (plant material + raw single-serving units count toward 2.5 oz; all other products count toward 15,000 mg). The report is right to distinguish this dispensing limit from the possession limit in 3796.221(B) (2.5 oz + 15 g extract, cumulative). Note 8-08(A)(2)(c) still cites former ORC 3780.36 — a stale cross-reference to flag, like 9-05's Chapter 3780 citation. Reciprocity statute confirmed: DCC "shall attempt in good faith to negotiate" where the other state's eligibility is substantially comparable and the other state recognises Ohio cards; if an agreement is entered, the out-of-state authorisation "shall be accepted and valid" with the same rights as an Ohio patient/caregiver. Whether any such agreement currently exists was not verified — re-check the DCC reciprocity list before republication. Possession/transfer limits confirmed at 3796.221(B)–(C) (cumulative 2.5 oz / 15 g; transfer only without remuneration, ≤ daily amount, at privately owned residential/agricultural property). Federal-land bar confirmed at 3796.24(H)(3). Hotel-room lawfulness remains Unverified — no statute or DCC guidance located.
Part 12, §12.6 landlord/tenantLandlord/tenant ORC 3796.24(F)–(G), (A)–(D), (H)–(I); "Local government may not prohibit or limit homegrown marijuana," ORC 3796.29Confirmed, with qualifiersORC 3796.24; ORC 3796.29(F) confirmed verbatim: patient/caregiver status "shall not be used as the sole or primary basis for rejecting the person as a tenant unless the rejection is required by federal law," but a landlord may prohibit in the lease (1) smoking/combustion/vaporisation consumption in the premises/common areas and (2) homegrown cultivation. (G) public-benefits protection (except unemployment compensation under Chapter 4141, incl. 3796.28(B)) confirmed. (A) professional-licence, (B) children, (C) medical care/transplant, (D) forfeiture, (H)(4)–(5) public-place accommodation, (H)(6) IRB research, (I) contract enforceability — all confirmed. Correction to the report's framing: (F) protects registered patients/caregivers only; the report is right to flag adult-use (non-patient) tenant-rejection protection as Unverified — do not extend (F) to adult-use consumers. Homegrown: current text is narrower than the shorthand — (A) allows a municipality/township to prohibit or limit the number of licensed cultivators, processors or dispensaries; (B)(2) bars ordinances that prohibit/limit any activity authorised under Chapter 3796 except as expressly permitted under (A) — homegrown is such an authorised activity, but the report should quote (B)(2), not a freestanding "may not prohibit homegrown" sentence. (B)(1) grandfathering and (B)(3) IRB research also confirmed. Eviction mechanics under ORC Chapter 5321 remain unopened — Unavailable.

Part 12, §§12.8–12.9 veterinary, schoolsNo Ohio veterinary cannabis statute/rule; pet CBD guidance (FDA non-approval, NASC/AAFCO); no Ohio K-12 medical-cannabis administration statute; 500-ft buffer; public-place accommodation; minor-patient rulesCorrected (buffer); Unverified (veterinary and K-12 absences)ORC 3796.30; ORC 3796.24Buffer correction: current ORC 3796.30 (SB 56, eff. 20 March 2026) (A) bars a licensed cultivator/processor/dispensary/laboratory within 500 ft of the boundaries of a parcel with a school, church, public library, public playground or public park; (B) says DCC shall deny a relocation request that would put a facility within 500 ft — not "licence revocation," as the superseded 3 Oct 2023 version/Run 1 summary had it; (C) grandfathers a facility already holding a certificate when the protected facility arrives/moves within 500 ft; (D) IRB-research exemption. Ohio Cannabis and Hemp — Run 1, Parts 0–6 — Combined Report

Date accessed: 28 October 2026. Federal baseline as given in the commission (see Part 0-1 file). This combined file concatenates the three Run 1 research tracks in order. Research notes/gaps for each track are at the end of each part file.

Ohio Cannabis and Hemp — Run 1, Parts 0–1 ONLY

Scope: Parts 0 (Headlines) and 1 (Laws) only. Parts 2–6 are NOT covered in this file and are left for a separate run. Date accessed for all facts below: 28 October 2026 (browser crawls dated 29 Oct 2026 UTC are the same research session; Ohio local date 28 Oct 2026). Method note: Official Ohio Revised Code (ORC) chapter pages on codes.ohio.gov were opened and read directly. Where a fact rests only on a secondary source, that is stated and the fact is flagged. Every law statement below distinguishes original Issue 2 text from later legislative amendment, as required. Issue 2 was an initiated statute, not a constitutional amendment, so the General Assembly could — and did — rewrite it.

Federal baseline applied (given, not re-researched)

  • State-licensed MEDICAL marijuana and FDA-approved products moved to Schedule III effective 28 April 2026 (91 FR 22714). All adult-use marijuana remains Schedule I. The broader 2024 rescheduling proposal is not final.
  • IRS §280E is generally lifted for Schedule III medical activity; adult-use remains fully subject to §280E.
  • Hemp: PL 119-37 §781 takes effect 12 November 2026, but PL 119-103 §2019 limits it until 11 December 2026. After 11 December 2026 the full total-THC hemp definition and the 0.4 mg total THC per container cap apply.
  • USDA enforcement of DEA-registered lab testing for hemp is delayed to 31 December 2026.
  • The federal medical marijuana appropriations rider runs through 11 December 2026.
  • There is no federal cannabis banking law.

How the federal baseline interacts with Ohio — read this first

  1. Dual-licence split is the whole story in Ohio. Ohio's current code (ORC Chapter 3796 as amended by SB 56, see §1.2) authorises the same licensed cultivator, processor and dispensary to handle both medical and adult-use marijuana — e.g. ORC 3796.18(A)(2): "A licensed cultivator engaging in the activities authorized by this chapter shall do so respecting both medical marijuana and adult-use marijuana" (same language in 3796.19 and 3796.20). Most Ohio licensees are therefore dual. For federal purposes that single Ohio licence does NOT make adult-use product Schedule III. Only the marijuana that is "subject to a qualifying state-issued medical marijuana license" / dispensed as medical marijuana is Schedule III; product sold as adult-use, and any adult-use inventory, remains Schedule I and fully subject to §280E. A dual licensee must therefore split its activity — medical vs adult-use inventory, sales, revenue and deductions — for federal tax and scheduling purposes. The federal order itself, per secondary summaries of it, states it "does not constitute a final determination on federal tax liability for any particular business" — so the §280E relief for medical activity is general, not a business-specific ruling. Source for the federal split: task baseline; secondary confirmation: https://www.taftlaw.com/news-events/law-bulletins/dea-reschedules-fda-approved-and-state-licensed-medical-marijuana-to-schedule-iii/ and https://ayarlaw.com/irs-audits/irs-audit-marijuana-dispensary — accessed 28 Oct 2026. Ohio state-law flag: ORC 3796.01(C) as amended 20 Mar 2026 still reads: "Notwithstanding any conflicting provision of Chapter 3719. of the Revised Code or the rules adopted under it, for purposes of this chapter, marijuana is a schedule II controlled substance." Source: https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/chapter-3796 — accessed 28 Oct 2026. That is a state-law classification for Chapter 3796 purposes; it has NOT been updated in the text read to Schedule III, and it does not override the federal Schedule III / Schedule I split above. [VERIFY — contradiction to reconcile in Run 2 / with tax counsel: whether Ohio intends to amend 3796.01(C), and how Ohio treats Schedule III medical marijuana for state controlled-substance purposes.]
  2. Ohio got to the federal hemp numbers first — and went further on sales channel. Ohio's SB 56 hemp definition (ORC 928.01(C)(4)(c), effective 20 Mar 2026) already excludes from "hemp" any final hemp-derived cannabinoid product with "Greater than four-tenths of a milligram combined total per container of total tetrahydrocannabinols, including tetrahydrocannabinolic acid" plus similar-effect cannabinoids — i.e. the same 0.4 mg per container figure as the post-11 Dec 2026 federal cap — and excludes synthetically produced / non-naturally-producible cannabinoids. The federal dates therefore do not create a new Ohio threshold in December 2026; they align federal law with a threshold Ohio already enacted in March 2026. The difference is channel: Ohio law, by removing those products from the definition of hemp, makes them "marihuana" under ORC 3719.01 / 928.01(J), which can then lawfully be possessed only as licensed dispensary marijuana or lawful homegrown marijuana (ORC 3796.221). In other words Ohio's March 2026 rule is already stricter in effect than the federal transition: there is no Ohio grace period running to 11 Dec 2026 for intoxicating hemp sold outside dispensaries, because Governor DeWine line-item vetoed SB 56's hemp-beverage grace period (see §1.5). After 11 Dec 2026, federal and Ohio law converge on total-THC + 0.4 mg/container, but Ohio enforcement does not wait for December. [VERIFY — the precise criminal penalty for an unlicensed sale of an intoxicating hemp product was stated in secondary sources as first-degree misdemeanour / fifth-degree felony on repeat; the ORC 928.99 penalty text read covers only reckless violation of 928.04 (licence) — the dispensary-channel sale penalty was not located in the primary text read in this run. Do not cite a penalty without re-checking ORC 3796.99 and any Chapter 3779 remnant.]
  3. No Ohio 280E decoupling was located. One secondary tax source states "Ohio has no state 280E decoupling" (https://greengrowthcpas.com/industries/cannabis/ohio-cannabis-accounting/ — accessed 28 Oct 2026). No Ohio statute decoupling from §280E for state income tax was found in this run. [VERIFY — confirm against Ohio Department of Taxation guidance before Run 2 taxes section.] If that is correct, a dual licensee's federal medical relief does not automatically flow through to Ohio state tax, and adult-use activity remains disallowed at both levels.

PART 0: HEADLINES

# Headline Source (accessed 28 Oct 2026)
H1 Chapter 3780 is gone. SB 56 (136th GA, Sen. Steve Huffman) repealed the entire voter-enacted adult-use Chapter 3780 effective 20 March 2026 and consolidated medical + adult-use into a rewritten Chapter 3796. Every current adult-use rule cited in this report is therefore a later legislative amendment (SB 56), not original Issue 2 text, unless expressly noted as carried over unchanged. https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/chapter-3796 (sections headed "Effective: March 20, 2026 / Latest Legislation: Senate Bill 56"); https://statusreport.lsc.ohio.gov/136/sb56?sort=Name (Signed 12/19/2025, line-item veto, Effective 03/20/2026)
H2 SB 56 signed 19 Dec 2025 with line-item vetoes; House 52–34 (19 Nov 2025, conference report), Senate 22–7 (9 Dec 2025, conference report). Operating appropriations effective 19 Dec 2025; substantive marijuana/hemp changes effective 20 Mar 2026. https://statusreport.lsc.ohio.gov/136/sb56?sort=Name; https://www.ohiosenate.gov/news/on-the-record/update-governor-signs-senate-bill-56-reforming-ohios-marijuana-and-intoxicating-hemp-laws
H3 Possession and home grow numbers UNCHANGED, but possession is now cumulative and source-restricted. Adults 21+ may possess 2.5 oz plant material + 15 g extract, cumulative across homegrown + dispensary marijuana (ORC 3796.221(B), SB 56). Home grow remains 6 plants per adult, 12 per residence (ORC 3796.04, SB 56). The new bite: lawful possession is limited in practice to marijuana obtained from an Ohio licensed dispensary or lawfully homegrown in Ohio; out-of-state-purchased marijuana falls outside the 3796.221 safe harbour. https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-3796.221; https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/chapter-3796 (§3796.04)
H4 Public smoking/vaping sharply narrowed. Smoking, combustion or vaporisation of adult-use/homegrown marijuana is now allowed only on privately owned real property used primarily for residential or agricultural purposes (ORC 3796.06(C)(2), SB 56); knowing consumption in a public place is prohibited (3796.04(C)(2)). Passenger smoking/vaping in a moving vehicle is a third-degree misdemeanour; operator is under OVI law (3796.99(A), SB 56). https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/chapter-3796 (§§3796.04, 3796.06, 3796.99)
H5 Intoxicating hemp effectively banned outside dispensaries from 20 Mar 2026. ORC 928.01 (SB 56) removes from "hemp" any final product over 0.4 mg combined total THC (incl. THCA) per container, any non-naturally-producible cannabinoid, and any naturally-producible cannabinoid synthesised/manufactured outside the plant. The enrolled SB 56 hemp-beverage carve-out (up to 5 mg THC beverages to 31 Dec 2026, former Chapter 3779) was line-item vetoed by Gov. DeWine. Secondary reporting and the Ohio Senate summary agree the veto made the ban immediate on 20 Mar 2026 rather than year-end. https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/chapter-928 (§928.01); https://www.ohiosenate.gov/news/on-the-record/update-governor-signs-senate-bill-56-reforming-ohios-marijuana-and-intoxicating-hemp-laws ("All intoxicating hemp products must be bought in a licensed marijuana dispensary following the governor's line-item veto"); Supreme Court filing summarising the veto: https://www.supremecourt.ohio.gov/pdf_viewer/pdf_viewer.aspx?pdf=999501.pdf&subdirectory=2026-0264%5CDocketItems&source=DL_Clerk
H6 Executive Order 2025-05D (DeWine, signed 8 Oct 2025, effective 14 Oct 2025, 12:01 a.m.) was the precursor, NOT current law. It declared an adulterated-consumer-product emergency under ORC 3715.74, ordered intoxicating hemp products off display / not for sale, and suspended ORC 119.03 rulemaking so the Dept. of Agriculture could amend OAC 901:14-1-01 and 901:14-2-01 by emergency rule, expiring 120 days from the emergency rules' effective date or on adoption through normal JCARR process, whichever sooner. It was challenged in Franklin County (25CV008646) and, per secondary reports, paused by a judge — and in any event it is now superseded by SB 56's statutory hemp definition. Do not cite EO 2025-05D as current law. https://cannabusiness.law/wp-content/uploads/Signed-EO-2025-05D.pdf; https://www.dinsmore.com/publications/ohio-bans-intoxicating-hemp-products-for-90-days/ (8 Oct 2025 order, 90-day framing in secondary summary — note the signed order itself says 120 days for the emergency rules; see Research Notes R-7)
H7 Referendum to repeal SB 56 FAILED. Ohioans for Cannabis Choice launched a veto referendum; secondary sources agree it needed ~248,000–250,000 valid signatures from at least 44 of 88 counties by 19 Mar 2026 (the day before SB 56 took effect), the Attorney General initially rejected summary language in January 2026, and organisers suspended the effort 18 Mar 2026. SB 56 therefore took effect as enacted (as vetoed). No referendum is pending on the evidence found. https://thehazeconnect.com/blogs/learn/ohio-hemp-law-sb-56-thca-2026; https://thefostoriafreepress.com/columbus-analysis-ohio-lets-households-grow-12-cannabis-plants-but-keep-only-2-5-ounces-per-person-how-sb-56-boxed-in-home/

Ohio Judge Helmick 14-day TRO 15 June 2026 for 10 hemp companies, converted to a preliminary injunction 13–18 July 2026 on dormant Commerce Clause grounds; second TRO 7 Aug 2026 for 14 more companies. These injunctions are plaintiff-specific on the reporting; they do NOT restore general retail sale of intoxicating hemp in Ohio. PART 1: LAWS

1.1 Legal status — what is legal for adults

Both medical and adult-use marijuana are legal in Ohio under state law, for different populations, under one chapter since 20 Mar 2026.

HB 523 (131st GA, 2016), as amended; now administered under rewritten Ch. 3796 https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/chapter-3796 (§§3796.01, 3796.08, 3796.22)

Home grow Legal, 6/adult, 12/residence, primary residence only, enclosed/secured, not visible from a public space, not at a child-care home / halfway-house-type facility / rental that bans it (3796.04). No sale, no profit, no growing on behalf of another, no hydrocarbon extraction (3796.04(B)). Issue 2 (former 3780.28) carried into 3796.04 by SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026 — numbers unchanged https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/chapter-3796 (§3796.04)
Gifting / transfer Only the 3796.221(A)(4) transfer: without remuneration, ≤2.5 oz plant / ≤15 g extract to the same adult-use consumer in the same day, on privately owned residential/agricultural property. Any other giving/selling/transfer by a non-licensee is trafficking under ORC 2925.03 via 3796.99(F). SB 56 rewrite of Issue 2 gifting https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-3796.221; https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-3796.99
Public use Illegal. Knowing consumption of adult-use/homegrown marijuana in a public place is prohibited (3796.04(C)(2)); smoking/combustion/vaporisation is confined to privately owned residential/agricultural property (3796.06(C)(2)); a public-place operator must not knowingly permit it (3796.04(C)(3)). Medical smoking/combustion was already prohibited (3796.06(C)(1)); medical vaporisation is caught by the same private-property rule (3796.06(C)(2)). SB 56 (narrower than Issue 2) https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/chapter-3796 (§§3796.04, 3796.06)
Use in a vehicle Operator: OVI law (ORC 4511.19 etc.) applies. Passenger smoking/vaping while the operator is operating or in physical control: third-degree misdemeanour (3796.99(A)(2)). Operating while under the influence is never authorised (3796.04(E), 3796.221(E), 3796.22(D)). SB 56 https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-3796.99
Federal land Chapter 3796 does not permit use/possession/administration on federal land in Ohio (3796.24(H)(3)). HB 523 origin, retained by SB 56 https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/chapter-3796 (§3796.24)
Under-21 No person under 21 shall knowingly purchase, use or possess adult-use/homegrown marijuana (3796.06(G)); no person shall knowingly give/sell/distribute it to a person under 21 (3796.06(F)). Medical patients may be under 21 only via the medical programme (parent/guardian + caregiver — see §1.4; minor-patient detail [VERIFY — age floor and consent rule in OAC 1301:18-10, not opened]). SB 56 / HB 523 https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/chapter-3796 (§3796.06)

What is NOT legal (common misconceptions, current law): - Buying marijuana in Michigan (or any other state) and possessing it in Ohio — outside the 3796.221 safe harbour, treated as possession under ORC 2925.11 via 3796.99(D). Secondary analysis is unanimous on this reading; the statute's safe harbour is expressly limited to a consumer "who obtains adult-use marijuana from a licensed dispensary" (3796.221(A)) plus homegrown under 3796.04. - Selling or profiting from homegrown marijuana; growing for another person (3796.04(B)(4)–(5)). - Keeping a full harvest: harvested (cut) flower counts toward the 2.5 oz cap even if the plants were lawfully grown; only seeds, live plants and clones being cultivated under 3796.04 are excluded from the plant-material cap (3796.221(B)(1)). A lawful 6–12 plant garden can therefore produce a harvest that exceeds the possession cap — this is a real statutory trap noted by commentators, not a drafting error in this report. [Flag for Run 2 consumer section.] - Adult-use delivery to a consumer's home: the dispensary delivery power in 3796.20(A)(1)(e) is expressly "delivery of medical marijuana" under rules adopted under 3796.03; 3796.03(B)(15)(b) likewise provides only for "Delivery of medical marijuana by a licensed dispensary." No adult-use delivery power exists in the statute read. Whether medical delivery rules are actually operational (vs merely authorised) is [VERIFY — DCC delivery rules, Part 4/11]; secondary sources in 2026 variously say medical delivery is "authorised subject to rules" and "not operating / pickup only." Do not state it is operating without a DCC source.

1.2 Every state statute and regulation — citation, summary, verbatim operative text, last amended, link, Issue 2 vs amendment

A. Constitutional / initiative background

  • Issue 2 (2023) — initiated statute, passed 7 Nov 2023, effective 7 Dec 2023, creating former ORC Chapter 3780. Because it was a statute, the General Assembly retained full power to amend it. It is no longer in force as a chapter: SB 56 repealed Chapter 3780 effective 20 Mar 2026. Citations to "3780.xx" in older guidance are therefore historic.
  • Issue 3 (2015) — failed ballot measure; out of scope for Part 1 law text, covered in Run 2 Part 9 history. Do not confuse with Issue 2.

B. ORC Chapter 3796 — Marijuana Control Law (current, unified medical + adult-use chapter)

Chapter page: https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/chapter-3796 — accessed 28 Oct 2026. All sections below are "Effective: March 20, 2026 / Latest Legislation: Senate Bill 56 – 136th General Assembly" unless stated otherwise. That means every section below is a later legislative amendment (SB 56) in its current form, even where it carries over Issue 2 or HB 523 substance.

Section Plain-English summary Verbatim operative text (excerpt) Last amended / origin
3796.01 Definitions Defines marijuana (via 3719.01), medical vs adult-use vs homegrown marijuana as mutually exclusive categories; adult-use consumer = 21+; qualifying conditions list (see §1.4); "division of marijuana control" = Division of Cannabis Control. "(9) 'Adult-use marijuana' means marijuana that is cultivated, processed, dispensed, or tested for, or possessed or used by, an adult-use consumer, in accordance with this chapter." … "(17) 'Homegrown marijuana' means marijuana cultivated, grown, processed, or possessed by an adult-use consumer in accordance with section 3796.04" … "(C) Notwithstanding any conflicting provision of Chapter 3719. … for purposes of this chapter, marijuana is a schedule II controlled substance." SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026; qualifying-condition list originates HB 523
3796.02 Establishment Establishes the Division of Cannabis Control in the Dept. of Commerce under the Superintendent of Marijuana Control (ORC 121.04); division licenses cultivators, processors, dispensaries, labs, registers patients/caregivers, administers the programme. "There is hereby established a division of cannabis control in the department of commerce … The division shall provide for the licensure of marijuana cultivators, processors, retail dispensaries, and laboratories that test marijuana." SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026 (division originally created for medical by HB 33, 2023 — see §1.4 transfer note)
3796.03 Adoption of rules DCC must adopt Chapter 119 rules: applications/fees, eligibility + disqualifying offences, cultivator numbers, renewal, suspension, patient/caregiver registration, dispensary employee training, 90-day supply by form/THC, paraphernalia, ID cards, child-attractive forms, veteran/indigent assistance, testing, online/mobile ordering (both) and medical-only delivery, anti-inducement (no gifts/samples to induce business), non-marijuana ingredients. "(B)(15) Establish standards and procedures for both of the following: (a) Online and mobile ordering of adult-use and medical marijuana by a licensed dispensary; (b) Delivery of medical marijuana by a licensed dispensary or an agent of a licensed dispensary to a registered medical marijuana patient or caregiver." SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026
3796.031 Closed-loop payment Director of Commerce may adopt rules for a state closed-loop payment system for patients/caregivers/licensees (anti-diversion, anti-crime purpose; data accessible to Board of Pharmacy and law enforcement incl. FinCEN). Permissive, not stated to be operating — [VERIFY whether any such system exists]. See chapter text. HB 523, eff. 8 Sept 2016 — not amended by SB 56 (surviving HB 523 text)
3796.032 Research carve-out Chapter does not authorise DCC to oversee/limit marijuana research at a state university, academic medical centre or private R&D organisation approved by a listed federal agency (AHRQ, NIH, NAS, CMS, DoD, CDC, VA, DEA, FDA, NIH-recognised board). "This chapter does not authorize the division of cannabis control to oversee or limit research conducted at a state university, academic medical center, or private research and development organization that is related to marijuana and is approved by [a federal agency…]" SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026
3796.04 Home grow See §1.1 / §1.3. "(a) Not more than six homegrown marijuana plants are cultivated or grown by each adult-use consumer; (b) Not more than twelve homegrown marijuana plants are cultivated or grown at a single residence; (c) Cultivation … only within a secured closet, room, greenhouse, or other enclosed area … that prevents access by individuals under twenty-one years of age, and which is not visible by normal unaided vision from a public space" SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026; substance from Issue 2 former 3780.28
3796.05 Numbers; testing DCC considers population, patient numbers, consumer numbers for cultivator numbers; ≤400 dispensaries statewide; provisional dispensary licence revocable if no certificate of operation in 18 months (+ up to two 6-month good-faith extensions); geographic distribution must not oversaturate; no new/relocated dispensary within 1 mile of another dispensary or at a Chapter 4303 liquor-permit premises; ownership cap: ≤8 dispensaries, ≤1 cultivator, ≤1 processor per person; testing standards (when, minimum amount, uniformity, reporting). "(B)(1) Not more than four hundred licensed dispensaries shall be permitted to operate in this state at any one time." … "(C) No person shall own or operate more than eight licensed dispensaries, more than one licensed cultivator, or more than one licensed processor license at any time." SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026 — 400 cap, 1-mile rule and ownership cap are SB 56 additions, not Issue 2 (Issue 2 directed biennial consideration of additional licences)
3796.06 Forms; methods; potency; storage Medical forms: oils, tinctures, plant material, edibles, patches, + any other DCC-approved form. Adult-use forms: all medical forms + extracts, drops, lozenges, smoking/combustible, vaporisation, beverages, pills, capsules, suppositories, oral pouches/strips, oral/topical sprays, salves, lotions/cosmetics, inhalers, seeds, live plants, clones, pre-rolls. Child-attractive forms prohibited; no human/animal/fruit likeness. Potency: 35% plant material, 70% extracts for both medical and adult-use, except DCC may by Chapter 119 rule increase extract limits and set per-serving/per-package limits (3796.06(E)(3)) — the legal basis for the 90% rule in Oct 2026. No sale/gift to under-21; under-21 purchase/use/possession prohibited. Edibles must be stored in original packaging at all times when not actively in use (3796.06(H)) — SB 56 addition. "(E)(1) … the tetrahydrocannabinol content of medical marijuana dispensed or sold … shall not exceed: (a) Thirty-five per cent for plant material; (b) Seventy per cent for extracts." … "(E)(3) The division may adopt rules … that do either or both of the following: (a) Increase the [THC] content limits for extracts …; (b) Establish [THC] content limits … by content per serving or per package." SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026; forms list carried from Issue 2 former 3780.04 + HB 523, with pre-rolls etc. added; potency caps and edible-storage rule are SB 56
3796.061 Petition for form/method Any person may petition DCC for a new medical form/method (not smoking/combustion); DCC consults experts, decides, decision final; rules under Ch. 119. See chapter text. SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026
3796.062 Transportation Only adult-use/medical/homegrown marijuana may be transported in a motor vehicle. Dispensary marijuana: original unopened packaging, or if opened, in the trunk (or behind last upright seat / area not normally occupied and not easily accessible if no trunk). Homegrown: trunk / behind-last-seat rule (no original-packaging alternative). Same rule for paraphernalia. "(B) No person shall knowingly transport medical marijuana or adult-use marijuana in a motor vehicle unless … (1) … in the original, unopened packaging …; (2) If previously opened, … stored in the trunk …" SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026 — new, stricter than Issue 2
3796.07 Electronic database (seed-to-sale) DCC shall establish/maintain an electronic database monitoring adult-use + medical marijuana "from its seed source through its cultivation, processing, testing, and dispensing"; may contract out; updates instantaneously; licensee must submit information DCC determines necessary; data confidential, not a public record under ORC 149.43; no identification of a specific consumer/patient; aggregate/summary release allowed. Vendor name (Metrc) is NOT in the statute — see §1.7. "The division of cannabis control shall establish and maintain an electronic database to monitor adult-use and medical marijuana from its seed source through its cultivation, processing, testing, and dispensing." SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026 (substance from Issue 2 former 3780.05 + HB 523)
3796.08 Registration Patient/caregiver applies to Board of Pharmacy until 180 days after 3 Oct 2023, thereafter to DCC; physician (or delegate) submits on patient's/caregiver's behalf; application must certify bona fide relationship, qualifying-condition diagnosis, 12-month drug-database report requested, risks/benefits explained; names of caregiver(s)/patient(s); if complete, DCC registers and issues ID card; registration expires per rules, renewable; information confidential, not a public record, shareable with a dispensary only to confirm valid registration. "(A)(1) Until one hundred eighty days following October 3, 2023, a patient … shall apply to the state board of pharmacy … On and after one hundred eighty days following October 3, 2023, a patient … shall apply to the division of cannabis control" SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026; transfer mechanism originates HB 33 (2023) — see §1.4
3796.09 Cultivator/processor/lab licence Application per location; DCC evaluates/prioritises on eligibility, suitability, ability; eligibility includes criminal-records check (3796.12), no lab ownership/compensation or shared officers/employees (cultivator/processor), 500 ft from school/church/library/playground/park, tax compliance, liquid capital/financial responsibility, municipality/township has not prohibited it, no false/misleading application, fee paid. If eligible applicants exceed licences: impartial evidence-based ranking (business, operations, security, financial, principal place, location, jobs/economic development, environmental, employment practices, criminal/civil history). Lottery grouping (highly exceeds / exceeds / meets / does not meet; exceeds = double odds vs meets; highly exceeds = double vs exceeds; does-not-meet ineligible). ≥15% of cultivator/processor/lab licences to entities ≥51% owned and controlled by Ohio-resident US citizens who are Black/African American, American Indian, Hispanic/Latino, or Asian (if insufficient qualifying applications, usual procedures). Renewal not subject to ranking/lottery; renewal not deniable solely for proximity to other holders. Provisional licence not transferable. Unlicensed activity prohibited. "(C)(4) The applicant demonstrates that it will not be located within five hundred feet of a school, church, public library, public playground, or public park." … "(F) The division shall issue not less than fifteen per cent of cultivator, processor, or laboratory licenses to entities that are owned and controlled by [listed groups]" SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026; 15% set-aside originates HB 523
3796.10 Dispensary licence Same structure as 3796.09 plus: not within 1 mile of another licensed dispensary; not at a Chapter 4303 liquor-permit location; same 15% set-aside for retail dispensary licences; same ranking/lottery; provisional not transferable; unlicensed dispensing prohibited. "(C)(5) The applicant demonstrates that the proposed location or facility is not either of the following: (a) Located within one mile of another licensed dispensary; (b) Issued a permit under Chapter 4303. … to sell beer and intoxicating liquor" SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026 — 1-mile and liquor-permit bars are SB 56 additions
3796.11 Tax information Dept. of Taxation must, on DCC request for a pending application, provide tax-compliance / violations / penalties; Dept. may charge reasonable fee; information confidential, only to the applicant. See chapter text. SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026
3796.12 Criminal records check BCI (+ FBI if not 5-year Ohio resident, or at DCC discretion) check for administrators/daily-operation persons, owners/prospective owners, officers, board members; applicant pays BCI fee; report not a public record; licence denied if person fails to complete/forward forms or instruct BCI to report to DCC. See chapter text. SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026
3796.13 Employment (licence-holder staff) Person seeking employment with a license holder must comply with ORC 4776.01–4776.04 (criminal-records check); license holder shall not employ unless the report shows no disqualifying offence; DCC must set provisional-employment standards for exigent circumstances (evidence of 4776 compliance; ≤3 months, renewable once for 3 months); DCC may use instant background checks. This is about licensee employees, not general employment protection — see §1.8 for the separate employer-rights section. "(A) Each person seeking employment with a license holder shall comply with sections 4776.01 to 4776.04 … such a license holder shall not employ the person unless … [no] disqualifying offenses." SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026
3796.14 / 3796.15 Commerce authority; enforcement DCC may suspend (incl. without prior hearing), revoke, refuse to renew/issue, or civilly penalise for rule-specified reasons, under Ch. 119; dispensary summary suspension only on clear-and-convincing danger of immediate serious harm, lifted day 91 if no final order in 90 days after hearing; DCC + Ohio Investigative Unit (Dept. of Public Safety, ORC 5502.13) may inspect premises/records without prior notice; subpoena power; common-pleas contempt enforcement; Investigative Unit premises-inspection limits (license holder + DCC request or alleged crime, or invited by local law enforcement). DCC + Unit enforce the chapter; sealed product on suspension/revocation with danger finding, not disposed until appeals exhausted (court may order sale of perishables, proceeds to court). See chapter text. SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026
3796.16 Reciprocity DCC shall attempt in good faith to negotiate reciprocity with any other state where (a) that state's eligibility is substantially comparable and (b) that state recognises Ohio cards; shall not negotiate any other form of recognition; if an agreement is entered, the other state's authorisation is recognised and grants the same rights as an Ohio registration. No agreement was located in this run — out-of-state patients therefore have no recognised right on the evidence found. [VERIFY — DCC reciprocity page, Part 4/10.] "(A)(1) The division of cannabis control shall attempt in good faith to negotiate and enter into a reciprocity agreement with any other state …" SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026; substance HB 523
3796.17 Toll-free line DCC shall establish a toll-free line for adverse-reaction inquiries and information for consumers, patients, caregivers, health professionals; may contract out. See chapter text. SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026
3796.18 Cultivator licence (rights) Licensed cultivator (incl. pre-amendment holder) may cultivate medical + adult-use, deliver/transfer/sell to other license holders, purchase from other license holders, acquire seeds/clones/plants/genetics; must do so respecting both medical and adult-use; must not cultivate for personal/family/household use or on public land incl. state parks; must identify/package/label before delivery to processor/dispensary. Levels: Level I ≤100,000 sq ft cultivation area; Level II ≤15,000 sq ft (as specified by DCC); expansions allowed up to the level maximum with DCC approval. No Level III in current text — SB 56 deleted it. "(D) The division of cannabis control shall issue the following types of cultivation licenses: (1) A level I cultivator license … not to exceed one hundred thousand square feet; (2) A level II cultivator license … not to exceed fifteen thousand square feet." SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026
3796.19 Processor licence May purchase from license holders, process into a 3796.06 form, deliver/transfer/sell to license holders, respecting both medical and adult-use; before delivery to a dispensary must package to child-resistant standard 16 C.F.R. 1700.15(b) (as of 8 Sept 2016), label THC + CBD content, comply with DCC packaging/labelling rules under 3796.03 and 3796.32. See chapter text. SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026
3796.20 Dispensary licence May purchase from license holders; dispense/sell medical per (B) and adult-use per (C); sell paraphernalia per rules; provide delivery of medical marijuana per 3796.03 rules; deliver/transfer/sell to license holders; must do so respecting both. Medical sale: only on current valid government ID + written recommendation from a physician holding a State Medical Board certificate to recommend under ORC 4731.30; report to drug database per ORC 4729.771; label with processor + dispensary name/address, patient (+ caregiver) name, physician name, directions if any, date dispensed, quantity/strength/kind/form; maintain adequate medical supply for typical patient demand. Adult-use sale: only to 21+ on government ID; no more per day than the legal possession amount (3796.221); label with processor + dispensary name/address, under-21 harmful-and-illegal statement, quantity/strength/kind/form. Dispensary staff must meet training rules; patient/consumer identifying information must not be made public; must prominently display under-21 statement + addiction/health-consequences information. "(C)(2) No licensed dispensary shall knowingly dispense or sell more than the amount of adult-use marijuana that may be legally possessed by an adult-use consumer under section 3796.221 … to the same adult-use consumer in the same day." SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026
3796.21 Laboratory licence Licensed lab (incl. pre-amendment holder) shall obtain marijuana from licensed cultivators/processors/dispensaries and test per DCC rules; when testing shall test for potency, homogeneity, and contamination and prepare a report. "(B) When testing medical marijuana or adult-use marijuana, a licensed laboratory shall do both of the following: (1) Test for potency, homogeneity, and contamination; (2) Prepare a report of the test results." SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026
3796.22 Patient rights Registered patient obtaining medical marijuana from a licensed dispensary may use it, possess it subject to (B), possess paraphernalia/accessories per rules; possession ≤ 90-day supply as specified in rules under 3796.03; not subject to arrest/prosecution for obtaining/using/possessing per chapter or possessing paraphernalia; does not authorise operating a vehicle etc. while under the influence. "(B) The amount of medical marijuana possessed by a registered patient shall not exceed a ninety-day supply, as specified in rules adopted under section 3796.03" SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026; 90-day concept HB 523
3796.221 Adult-use consumer rights See §1.1 verbatim. Note the opening words limit the safe harbour to a consumer "who obtains adult-use marijuana from a licensed dispensary" — homegrown protection is via 3796.04(D), subject to 3796.221(B)–(C). "(A) … an adult-use consumer who obtains adult-use marijuana from a licensed dispensary may do all of the following: (1) Use adult-use marijuana; (2) Possess adult-use marijuana, subject to division (B) …; (4) Transfer adult-use and homegrown marijuana to another adult-use consumer if [without remuneration, ≤ daily cap, on private residential/agricultural property]. (B) No person shall knowingly possess more than [2.5 oz plant / 15 g extract, cumulative]. (C) Except as expressly authorized under division (A)(4) …, no person other than a license holder shall knowingly give, sell, or transfer adult-use or homegrown marijuana to any other person, with or without remuneration." SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026 — replaces Issue 2 former 3780.36/3780.29 framework; cumulative cap + source limitation + private-property transfer condition are SB 56
3796.23 Caregiver rights Registered caregiver obtaining from a licensed dispensary may possess on behalf of a patient (≤90-day supply per patient, separate inventories per patient), assist in use/administration, possess paraphernalia per rules; not subject to arrest/prosecution for those acts; may not personally use unless also a registered patient (3796.23(D)). "(B) … If a caregiver provides care to more than one registered patient, the caregiver shall maintain separate inventories of medical marijuana for each patient." SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026; HB 523 origin
3796.24 Liability / protections Licence holder (ORC 4776.01) not subject to professional discipline solely for marijuana-related professional activity. Medical use/possession/administration per chapter shall not be the sole/primary basis for child abuse/neglect/dependency adjudication (unless clear-and-convincing evidence child unsafe), parental-rights allocation, or parenting-time orders. Shall not disqualify from medical care or transplant list. Shall not be sole/primary reason for property forfeiture/seizure action. Patient/caregiver status is not sufficient basis for a field sobriety test or licence suspension (independent reasonable suspicion required). Tenant protection (medical only in this section): status shall not be sole/primary basis for rejecting as tenant unless federal law requires it — but a landlord MAY prohibit, if in the lease: (1) smoking/combustion/vaporisation consumption in the premises/common areas; (2) cultivation/growth of homegrown marijuana. Public-benefit protection: medical/adult-use/homegrown use/possession per chapter shall not disqualify from a state/local public benefit, except unemployment compensation under Ch. 4141 as prescribed by 3796.28(B). Chapter does NOT require a physician to recommend; does NOT permit use except as authorised; does NOT permit use on federal land; does NOT require a public place to accommodate use; does NOT prohibit a public place accommodating medical use except smoking/combustion/vaporisation; does NOT restrict IRB-approved university/medical-centre/private R&D research. Licence-related contracts are enforceable as public policy. "(F) … a person's status as a registered patient or caregiver shall not be used as the sole or primary basis for rejecting the person as a tenant unless the rejection is required by federal law. This division does not prohibit a landlord from prohibiting either of the following, as long as such prohibition is included in the applicable lease agreement: (1) Consumption … by smoking, combustion, or vaporization; (2) Cultivation or growth of homegrown marijuana." SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026; tenant/benefit/child provisions HB 523 origin, extended by SB 56 to adult-use/homegrown in (G)
3796.27 Financial institutions Bank/trust/savings/credit union/money transmitter providing financial services to a compliant license holder is exempt from any Ohio criminal law an element of which could be proved by showing it provides services to a person who possesses/delivers/manufactures marijuana (incl. ORC 2925.05, 2923.01, 2923.03 as applied to Ch. 2925 violations), if the license holder complies with Ch. 3796 and applicable tax laws. DCC must on request provide license status, affiliates, unredacted application, sales/volume, compliance, violations/penalties (reasonable fee; confidential). State exemption only — no federal banking law exists (baseline), so federal risk remains. See chapter text. SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026
3796.28 Employer rights See §1.8 verbatim. See §1.8. SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026; extended from medical-only to all marijuana by SB 56
3796.29 Local limits Municipal legislative authority (ordinance) or township trustees (resolution) may prohibit or limit the number of licensed cultivators/processors/dispensaries in the municipality / unincorporated township territory — except they shall not adopt/enforce an ordinance/resolution that (1) prohibits/limits a holder that received a provisional licence or certificate of operation before SB 56's effective date, unless the ordinance/resolution was adopted before that date; (2) prohibits/limits any activity authorised under the chapter except as expressly permitted by (A); or (3) prohibits/limits IRB-approved research. Counties have no parallel power in this section. "(A) Except as otherwise provided in division (B) …, the legislative authority of a municipal corporation or a board of township trustees may adopt an ordinance or a resolution, to prohibit, or limit the number of, licensed cultivators, licensed processors, or licensed dispensaries within the municipal corporation or within the unincorporated territory of the township, respectively." SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026; substance HB 523, grandfather clause added by SB 56
3796.30 500-ft buffer No licensed cultivator/processor/dispensary/lab within 500 feet of the boundaries of a parcel with a school, church, public library, public playground or public park; relocation into the buffer must be denied; no relocation/closure required if the facility already held a certificate of operation when the protected facility moved in / was established; research exception. "(A) Except as provided in divisions (C) and (D) …, no licensed cultivator, licensed processor, licensed dispensary, or licensed laboratory shall be located within five hundred feet of the boundaries of a parcel of real estate having situated on it a school, church, public library, public playground, or public park." SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026; HB 523 origin (500 ft); SB 56 adds the 1-mile dispensary-to-dispensary rule separately in 3796.05/3796.10 — do not conflate
3796.31 No local cannabis taxes/fees Except as otherwise authorised in the Revised Code, no political subdivision shall levy (A) any tax/fee on license holders based on gross receipts or same/similar to a state tax/fee, or (B) any tax/fee/charge on license holders or their property not generally charged on other businesses. See chapter text. SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026
3796.32 Advertising/marketing DCC may adopt advertising rules to prevent false, misleading, minor-targeted/attractive, excessive-use, illegal-activity, obscene/indecent, use-depicting, or intoxicant-promoting ads; adult-use ad rules must be at least as stringent as the most stringent federal/state tobacco/alcohol ad laws/rules; DCC may audit published ads at any time; no packaging/advertising/marketing with cartoon / fictional / pop-culture figure whose target audience is children/youth; no ad asserting/suggesting adult-use marijuana has health/therapeutic benefits; no medical/adult-use ad within 500 ft of a school/church/library/playground/park parcel (except license-holder facility signage); no advertising using names/logos/signs/materials not submitted to and approved by DCC — DCC must approve/deny within 21 business days, silence = approval for names/logos/signs/materials under (G) (note: this 21-day deemed-approval is for (G) submissions; the OAC 1301:18-4-22 pre-approval rule for advertisements generally requires written approval before use — see §1.6, Research Note R-5). Violation: DCC may require cessation + enforcement. "(G)(1) No person shall advertise medical or adult-use marijuana using names, logos, signs, or materials that have not been submitted to, and approved by, the division in accordance with rules adopted under this section." SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026
3796.33 Equivalent licences A Chapter 3780 licence (pre-SB 56) is treated for all purposes as the equivalent Chapter 3796 licence; same person + same location: DCC shall merge them and treat as one licence (incl. expiration/renewal). This is the statutory conversion mechanism — no separate "dual licence application" is stated in the statute read. "(B) A license issued under Chapter 3780. … shall be treated, for all purposes, as the equivalent license under this chapter." SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026 — new conversion provision
3796.34 Drug misuse prevention DCC shall contract with a statewide nonprofit for cannabis/related-drug misuse prevention, education and public-awareness initiatives (data/evaluation/research-driven; ≥10% of funding raised privately by the nonprofit); initiatives may cover youth health effects, pregnancy risks, DUI dangers/consequences, employer/workforce resources; DCC oversees/evaluates and reports annually to the General Assembly under ORC 101.68. See chapter text. SB 56, eff. 20 Mar 2026 (former 3780.37, amended and renumbered)
3796.40 Excise tax See Part 2 headline H10; full distribution text was not fully read (chapter read cut off at 3796.40(E)).
